private_helper_review.finding: Squared-distance positivity follows from x!=a. The norm-square derivative and real-power chain rule give 2pS^(p-1) times the inner-product functional. Generic real Hilbert typing is sufficient, and no regularity premise is smuggled in.

private_helper_review.finding: The actual Riesz-gradient pairing identifies the derivative vector 2pS^(p-1)(x-a). Finite-dimensionality supplies the intended gradient setting.

private_helper_review.name: radial_second
private_helper_review.finding: The first-derivative formula is transferred by an eventual equality on a neighborhood avoiding a. Differentiating its scalar coefficient and linear dot factor gives 4p(p-1)S^(p-2)<x-a,e>^2+2pS^(p-1)<e,e>. It does not differentiate a merely pointwise identity.

private_helper_review.finding: Local C2 is proved before identifying second Frechet derivatives with directional second derivatives. The genuine Mathlib orthonormal trace and Parseval sum produce 4p(p-1)S^(p-2)S+2pS^(p-1)finrank. No counterfeit Laplacian is introduced.

This is a literal equality, not a replacement kernel definition. Its totalized equality also holds at the pole, though derivatives are used only away from it.

private_helper_review.finding: The norm-square Frechet derivative, its constant bilinear derivative and the orthonormal trace yield gradient -2x and Laplacian -2finrank, including x=0. Constant-subtraction regularity is derived internally.

private_helper_review.finding: Uses the actual factors u=1-||x||^2 and v=S^(-n/2). Their local C2 conditions discharge the canonical product theorem.
